claims.statement: EU policy promotes selective demolition and pre-demolition audits, but the Commission describes its protocol and audit guidance as non-binding and Polish law does not itself create a general paid-audit mandate.

Since 1 January 2025 Polish producers of construction and demolition waste must ensure separation of specified fractions, may contract the duty in writing to an authorized entity, and retain joint liability under the cited amendment.

The new Construction Products Regulation covers used products and future harmonized specifications, while products directly reused in a construction work are not considered placed on the market again; status and conformity therefore depend on the route and product class.

JRC evidence places pre-demolition audit cost around EUR 3000-5000 for demolition projects up to EUR 300000 and says effectiveness and economic benefit remain uncertain, especially for small projects.
Concular already combines pre-deconstruction audits, AI-assisted inventory, marketplace distribution, logistics, and optional insured or warranted installation, closely matching the proposed offer.

Marketplace evidence is mixed: Greyn offers free listing and charges only on sale, while RAEDIFICARE advertises no sales commission and reported EUR 125000 across 175 orders in 2024, about EUR 714 per order.

contrary_evidence: Pre-demolition audit guidance is non-binding and JRC found no direct effectiveness evidence for economic modelling.
JRC says small projects can face disproportionate administrative burden and EEA notes low-cost virgin inputs, weak standards, and quality doubts.
Concular already provides the integrated audit, inventory, marketplace, logistics, and insurance stack.
Greyn's free listing and RAEDIFICARE's no-commission model constrain marketplace take rates; RAEDIFICARE's reported average order value is low.
Used components can cross construction-product conformity and waste-law boundaries, and waste-market intermediaries enter BDO registration and recordkeeping scope.
A planned EU digital pre-demolition data platform could expand demand while commoditizing inventory data and crowding out a standalone exchange.

economics.acquisition_route: Win one demolition contractor and one property owner as design partners, screen their forward pipeline, and accept only sites whose recoverable-value estimate exceeds audit and coordination cost.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The original scale arithmetic remains possible but unvalidated: 250 projects at 18000 PLN blended revenue equals 4.5m PLN revenue; 25% EBITDA equals 1.125m PLN and a 5x multiple equals 5.625m PLN enterprise value. Reaching that throughput likely requires a full-time operating team and does not yet account for founder dilution, liabilities, or weak transaction values.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly if all field work, testing, removal, transport, storage, and waste handling are delegated to insured specialists.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 50-65% after contracted field survey and specialist review. The margin is an inference; destructive sampling, engineering review, hazardous-material work, removal, storage, transport, and warranty remain outside the fee or are passed through.
economics.payback: At 75000 PLN setup capital and 60% contribution margin, roughly ten projects at 12500 PLN revenue would recover setup cash before founder labour; the JRC reports audit costs around EUR 3000-5000 for demolitions up to EUR 300000, but not purchaser willingness to pay in Poland.
economics.pricing: Evidence-based starting test: 12000-25000 PLN for a scoped audit and coordination plan on a substantial site, plus 3-8% only for completed high-value product sales; low-value lots should be routed without commission dependence.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat depends on owner and demolition-contractor portfolios; individual salvage buyers and lots are irregular, and free or no-commission marketplaces limit standalone transaction pricing.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A proprietary record of local buyer acceptance criteria, removal yields, tested component classes, project timing, and lawful fallback routes improves triage and quoting
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial property owners and demolition contractors with sufficiently large renovation or demolition projects
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with a small number of demolition contractors, property managers, architects, and licensed waste operators rather than building an open consumer marketplace
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner mandate, pre-demolition inventory, document recovery, product-versus-waste triage, buyer matching, reservation, removal scheduling, and verified fallback routing without taking salvage inventory
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The owner or demolition contractor pays for a scoped resource audit and coordination plan; a separately disclosed success fee is earned only on a completed product sale or lawful waste route
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A demolition date is fixed and the owner must plan selective handling while potentially reusable components still have time to be documented and matched

founder_fit: Computer vision, structured inventories, and evidence reconciliation fit the founder's data skills.
A contractor-partner model can delegate site surveys, hazardous-material work, removal, storage, and transport.
Portfolio relationships are fewer and less public-facing than a consumer marketplace.
Project coordination and exception handling are operationally heavier than a pure software business and could strain the founder's part-time limit.
risks: Hazardous-material exposure and incomplete building records
BDO noncompliance if waste brokerage or possession is mishandled
Demolition delay, removal damage, storage, and transport overruns
Low lot value relative to audit and deconstruction cost
Powerful full-stack incumbents and free marketplace substitutes
Operational intensity incompatible with part-time scale

structure.commercial_archetype: Paid circularity audit and transaction coordination service
structure.control_point: The owner-authorized inventory and reservation window before deinstallation or waste classification closes reuse options
structure.critical_dependency: Clear title and product-versus-waste status for every lot, safe removal evidence, and licensed BDO-compliant partners whenever material is waste

thesis: Obtain an owner mandate early enough to inventory a building, recover documents, classify each lot as a directly reusable product or a regulated waste stream, and coordinate reservations and removal before demolition. Sell a paid audit and coordination service rather than relying on marketplace commission. The policy direction and Polish sorting duty support the workflow, but audits are not generally mandated in Poland, used-product conformity varies, waste brokerage can enter BDO scope, and established European operators already combine audits, marketplaces, logistics, and insured installation.
title: Owner-Mandated Pre-Demolition Reuse Brokerage
uncertainties: Polish owner willingness to grant access and pay before demolition procurement is fixed
Recoverable product value and buyer density by component class and region
Which lots remain products, become waste, or satisfy end-of-waste criteria
Engineering, testing, warranty, and insurer requirements for structural components
Field-survey productivity and total specialist cost in Poland
Whether reservation deposits change demolition schedules or merely add coordination
Repeat project volume available from three local contractors
Whether proposed EU digital audit infrastructure becomes mandatory and how Poland implements it
